This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 25,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic Shankarappa V vs Basappa on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147669444/

sentences.text:
The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 24.08.2020 at about 6.20 a.m, when the Petitioner was proceeding on his Honda Dio bearing Reg.No.KA53ER 8993 and when he reached near Doddadunnasandra Village, Krishnappa Service Station NH207 road, then, one Tractor bearing Reg. No.KA06B4083 and Water Tanker bearing SCCH 15 3 MVC No.3652/2020 Reg.No.KA06B4084 driven by its driver came in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Petitioner.
Due to which the Petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to RKB Sanjeevini hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.

He had spent more than Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as House Keeping at TCS and also working at ISS Facility Service and was earning 14,723/ and Rs.11,095/
per month.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tractor bearing Reg. No.KA06B4083 and Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06B4084 by its driver.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is SCCH 15 4 MVC No.3652/2020 the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Objection statement to the main Petition.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement contended that the Petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, it has denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.

Further it contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and SCCH 15 5 MVC No.3652/2020 effective driving license and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it contended that present owner one Raju S/o Krishnappa was not made as party to the proceedings.
The said Raju is the owner of the vehicle as on the date of the accident.
The Respondent No.1 has sold the offending vehicle to one Raju who is the present owner as per the policy records.
Further it contended that, the Tractor bearing Reg. No.KA06B4083 and Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06B4084 was not having valid permit as on the date of the accident.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner and has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

6. On the rival Pleadings my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
Shankarappa V vs Basappa on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147669444/
2 ISSUES 1.

sentences.text: Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Tractor and SCCH 15 6 MVC No.3652/2020 Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06B4084 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
3. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

4. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 9 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P9.
Further, he examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 8 documents at Ex.10 to 18 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 examined two witnesses as RW.1 and RW.2 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.R1 to 3 and closed its side evidence.

The learned counsel for the Petitioner has relied on the following decisions:
1. 2023 ACJ 1952, High Court of Karnataka, between G. Shivaputhra Vs. P.
Shanthamma and others 2. MFA No.9827 of 2012 (WC), High Court of Karantaka, between The New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Smt. Sadhika & others.

1. MFA No.6154/2019 (MVD), High Court of Karnataka, between Hemalatha @
Hema @ Hemavathi & others Vs. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd., &
another.

Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the written Arguments filed by the Petitioner and depositions, documents exhibited, citations and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
SCCH 15 8 MVC No.3652/2020 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 :

As per the Final Order, for the following :
Shankarappa V vs Basappa on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147669444/
3 REASONS 10. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tractor bearing Reg. No.KA06B4083 and Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06B4084 by its driver.

sentences.text: 11. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tractor bearing Reg. No.KA06B4083 and Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06B4084 by its driver.

12. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 9 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 and he has reiterated the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.3652/2020 Petition averments in his Chiefaffidavit.

Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar, IMV report, Wound Certificate, Charge sheet, Discharge summary,
Medical bills and Aadhaar card.

13. Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P 1 & 2 are the True copies of the FIR &
Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Gangadhar, the Anugondanahalli Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06B 4084 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the true copy of Spot Mahazar which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex. P.4 is the IMV report which shows that the said accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.

Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate of the Petitioner which shows the following injuries:
1) Left knee anterior crusciate ligament, posterior crusiate ligament lateral meniscus tear SCCH 15 10 MVC No.3652/2020 2) Left shoulder acrmio clavicular joint disruption 14.
As per the opinion of the Doctor, said injuries are grievous in nature.

Ex.P.6 is the True copy of the Charge sheet which has been submitted by the Sub Inspector of Police, Anugondanahalli Police Station against the driver of the offending Tractor bearing Reg. No.KA06B4083 and Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06B4084 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
15.

Upon going through the Chargesheet i.e., Ex.P6, Column No.17 reads as under :

Ex.P8 is the Medical bills.
Ex.P9 is the Aadhaar card.
Further he has examined Assistant Medical Record Officer by name Gaurav Chand as PW.2 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.P10 to 13.

Further, the Petitioner has examined Doctor by name Dr.
Avinash Parthasarathi as P.W.3 and got marked 6 documents at Ex.P.14 to 19.

PW.1 is subjected for cross examination, but, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.
17.

On the other hand the Respondent No.2 has examined its Manager by name S.
Narendran as RW.1 and got marked Policy Copy at Ex.R.1 and also examined H.C by name Jayaram as RW.2 and RW.2 got marked 2 documents at SCCH 15 12 MVC No.3652/2020 Ex.R.2 and Ex.R.3.
RW.2 has reiterated the investigation he made and submission of Chargesheet.
The evidence of RW.2 is also clear that the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, he submitted Charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tractor bearing Reg. No.KA 06B4083 and Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06B4084 by its driver and due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
18. Issue No.2 and 3: Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are inter linked with each other and to avoid the repetition of facts.

As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3652/2020 Wanter tanker vehicle by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
19. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 47 years.
The Petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card at Ex.P9, which shows his date of birth as 01.01.1973.
The accident has taken place on 24.08.2020.
Hence, at the time of accident, the Petitioner was aged about 48 years.

20. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, he was working as House Keeping at TCS and also working at ISS facility Sevice and was earning 14,723/ and Rs.11,095/
per month.
But, he has not produced any document in this regard.

Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.14,500/ per month Shankarappa V vs Basappa on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147669444/
5 for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
21. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the SCCH 15 14 MVC No.3652/2020 sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS
PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P5 issued by the Medical Officer of the RKB Sanjeevini hospital, Bengaluru shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries i.e.,
1) Left knee anterior crusciate ligament, posterior crusiate ligament lateral meniscus tear 2) Left shoulder acrmio clavicular joint disruption

As per the opinion of the Doctor,
the injuries are grievous in nature.

23. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding SCCH 15 15 MVC No.3652/2020 compensation of 40,000/
under this head would be just and reasonable.
II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
24. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of  20,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
25.
The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken treatment at RKB Sanjeevini hospital, Bengaluru.

Upon going through Ex.P.7  Discharge summary of RKB Sanjeevini hospital shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 24.08.2020 to 29.08.2020 Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 06 days.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 29,000/ under this head (@ 14,500/
per month ).

Shankarappa V vs Basappa on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147669444/
6 IV.

COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
27.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period,
the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 6,000/ (@ 100/ per day)
towards attendants charges, 6,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and 6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 18,000/ under this head.
SCCH 15 17 MVC No.3652/2020 V.COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :

28. The petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent Rs.3,00,000/
towards medical and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced medical bills and hospital bills at Ex.P8.
I have gone through the medical bills.
The acceptable medical bills comes to Rs.1,61,155/.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at 1,61,200/.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for 1,61,200/ under this head.
VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:

29. The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident,
he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. Avinash Parthasarathi as P.W.3 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by him.
Further, he assessed the whole body disability at 16%.
PW.3 got marked Disability Assessment Proforma, MRI films and Report at Ex.P14 to 19.
In the crossexamination, PW.3 has deposed that he is not the treated doctor and he examined the petitioner only for the purpose of assessment of disability and the Petitioner did not get fracture.
He did not refer the Petitioner to Medical Board and get opinion and he did not get opinion of the treated doctor.
He further deposed that the Petitioner can do his work with little difficulty.

Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.3 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 8%
would be just and proper.

Shankarappa V vs Basappa on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147669444/
7 SCCH 15 19 MVC No.3652/2020 31.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 13.

With multiplier of 13, income of 14,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to 1,80,960/ (14,500/ x 12 = 1,74,000/, 1,74,000/x 13 x 8/100 =
1,80,960/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 1,80,960/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
32.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  40,000 /
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/
3. Loss of income during the laid  29,000/ up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  18,000/ and conveyance SCCH 15 20 MVC No.3652/2020 5.

Medical expenses  1,61,200/
6. Loss of Future Income  1,80,960/ Total  4,49,160/
33.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of  4,49,160/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

34. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Offending Tractor bearing Reg. No.KA06B4083 and Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06B4084.
RW.1 got marked copy of Policy at Ex.R.1 which shows that the Policy was valid at the time of accident.
35. It is the contention of the Respondent No.2 that the offending vehicle did not had permit as on the date of the accident.
RW.1 also reiterated the said fact in his evidence.
In the crossexamination he denied the suggestions.

Respondent SCCH 15 21 MVC No.3652/2020 No.2 has also examined the Head Constable by name Jayaram as RW.2 who is an I.O. and said RW.2 has reiterated the investigation he made and submission of Charge Sheet.
In the chief examination he deposed that during the time of his investigation he found that the said Tractor does not had permit as on the date of accident.
Therefore he has also Charge sheeted for the offence punishable under Sec.192 of MV Act along with Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.

In Shankarappa V vs Basappa on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147669444/
8 the cross examination he denied the suggestions.

sentences.text:
Ex.P.6 is the Charge sheet which shows that after investigation the I.O. has submitted Charge sheet against the driver of the offending Tractor for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC and Sec.192 of MV Act.
36.

Though the Respondent No.2 has produced the Police notice and Reply at Ex.R.2 and Ex.R.3 it shows the name as one K. Raju and the policy as on the date of the accident stands in the name of Respondent No.1.
Moreover, the Respondent No.1 did not appear before the Tribunal, though SCCH 15 22 MVC No.3652/2020 notice served on him.
Therefore this tribunal is of the opinion that the Respondent No.1 the owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.

37. The learned counsel for the Petitioner has relied on the decision reported in 2023 ACJ 1952 between G. Shivaputhra Vs. P. Shanthamma & Others wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to held as under:
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, section 149(2) (a) (I)
(a) Motor Insurance - Permit - Liability of insurance company - Pay and recover order - Insurance Company examined officer from RTO who deposed that neither the offending autorickshaw was having a permit nor any application to obtain the same was filed -

entities.text: G. Shivaputhra Vs. P. Shanthamma & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Tribunal exonerated insurance company from liability -

Owner contended that policy was subsequently renewed without verifying whether permit has been obtained which shows that insurance company never intended to dispute its liability on the issue of permit -
It is not the case of owner that autorickshaw was having a permit -
Whether nonpossession of permit amounts to infraction on the part of owner and Tribunal rightly exonerated insurance company from liability -

Held: yes:
however, considering the object of the Act SCCH 15 23 MVC No.3652/2020 insurance company directed to pay compensation at the first instance and then recover the amount from ownerinsured.
38.
In the instant case also Charge sheet shows that the offending vehicle has plied without permit.
The Policy of the offending vehicle was valid at the time of accident.

Hence, by relying on the above said dictum of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, this Tribunal is of the opinion that at the first instance, it is necessary to direct the insurer i.e., Respondent No.2 to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner and thereafter, recover the same from the Respondent No.1 i.e., insured.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
39. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 to 3 , I proceed to pass the following:

9  ORDER  The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 4,49,160/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award SCCH 15 25 MVC No.3652/2020 amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Schedule bank for a period of three years.

The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
